body.statement: Consistency, armwise conditional exchangeability, and overlap imply that \(\mu_a\) is a version of \(x\mapsto\mathbb E_P[Y_a\mid X=x]\) for each \(a\in\{0,1\}\). Under the known uniform design and Hölder effect condition, \(\tau\) is the unique continuous representative of the almost-everywhere conditional causal contrast \(x\mapsto\mathbb E_P[Y_1-Y_0\mid X=x]\). Hence \(\theta(P)=\tau_P(x_0)\) is identified as the value at \(x_0\) of that continuous representative.
body.justification: The continuous-version convention makes pointwise CATE identification well posed under a continuous design.
body.gap: Kennedy et al. use the same causal model; this lemma makes explicit the continuous representative required at a probability-zero covariate point.
body.consumer: It permits every testing separation below to be interpreted as a separation of identified pointwise causal effects.
